'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***The [[Israeli Defense Forces|IDF]] claims to have discovered a [[Hamas]] [[data center]] under [[UNRWA]]'s [[Gaza Strip]] headquarters. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/unrwa-head-says-agency-was-in-dark-about-hamas-center-under-gaza-hq-israel-you-knew/ (Times of Israel)]
**[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)]]
***[[Red Sea crisis]]
****Seventeen [[Houthi movement|Houthi]] fighters are killed during [[airstrike]]s launched by the [[United States]] and the [[United Kingdom]] in [[Yemen]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/2/10/yemens-houthis-say-17-rebels-killed-in-us-led-attacks (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 offensive (2022–present)|M23 offensive]]
***Tens of thousands of people flee to [[Goma]], the capital of the [[DR Congo]]'s [[North Kivu]] province, as [[March 23 Movement|M23 rebels]] advance towards the city. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-68255614 (BBC News)]
*[[Somali civil war (2009–present)|Somali civil war]]
**Four [[United Arab Emirates Army|Emirati soldiers]] and a [[Bahrain Defence Force|Bahraini military officer]] are killed, while ten other people are injured, when a soldier [[Mass shooting|opens fire]] at a [[military base]] in [[Mogadishu]], [[Somalia]], before being killed in the ensuing [[shootout]]. [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility. [https://apnews.com/article/somalia-shabab-emirates-bahrain-militant-attack-05cea538d50595b254a4b50131d84a1a (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[France]]'s [[Électricité de France|EDF]] shuts down two [[Nuclear reactor|nuclear reactors]] due to a fire at the [[Chinon Nuclear Power Plant]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/frances-edf-shuts-down-two-nuclear-reactors-after-fire-chinon-plant-2024-02-10/ (Reuters)]
*A [[Eurocopter EC130]] [[helicopter]] crashes near [[Nipton]], [[California]], [[United States]], killing all the six people on board, including [[Nigeria]]n banker [[Herbert Wigwe]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/helicopter-leaving-palm-springs-crashes-near-baker-search-for-passengers-continues/ (CBS News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023–2024 Senegalese protests]]
**Violent protests occur in [[Senegal]] following an announcement by President [[Macky Sall]] that [[2024 Senegalese presidential election|presidential elections]] have been delayed from  February 25 to December 15. [https://news.sky.com/video/violent-protests-erupt-in-senegal-after-president-postpones-elections-13068108 (Sky News)]
*[[2024 Pakistani general election]]
**Despite [[Imran Khan]]'s lead, [[Nawaz Sharif]] claims victory amid allegations of [[Pakistan Armed Forces|military]]-led rigging of the election. [https://time.com/6693147/pakistan-election-results-imran-khan-pti-military/ (''Time'')]
*[[President of Hungary]] [[Katalin Novák]] resigns one week after news media revealed that she had pardoned a person who had been convicted of aiding in [[child sex abuse]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/hungarian-president-novak-resigns-over-sex-abuse-case-pardon-2024-02-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 AFC Asian Cup]]
**In [[association football]], hosts [[Qatar national football team|Qatar]] win their second consecutive [[Asian Cup]] title after defeating [[Jordan national football team|Jordan]] 3–1 in [[2023 AFC Asian Cup final|the final]]. [[Akram Afif]] earns a [[hat-trick (association football)|hat-trick]]—all scored from [[penalty kick]]s. [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/feb/10/qatar-jordan-asian-cup-final-match-report (Reuters via ''The Guardian'')]
